segments.t: Eleonora threatens to fire Mikhail Jekovich unless he restores order immediately, and sentences Senya and Fedya to work a week without pay and two weeks without days off. Mikhail immediately calls a buyer to get rid of the pony.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Quickly restore order in the hotel!' With the kitchen and chaos at stake, Eleonora reacts without holding back.

'Otherwise I will throw you out of here.' Admitting that otherwise she will throw Ainura out of here shows Eleonora being honest for a change. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.

'And you two listen to me.' With the kitchen and chaos in play, Eleonora keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Even in the middle of the drama, she keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'You will work a week with no salary at all.' Once Ainura will work a week with no salary at all, Eleonora can finally tell Ainura what she means.
'And two weeks without days off.' Around the kitchen and chaos, Eleonora sets a calm, everyday tone with Ainura.

'That is it, get out of here quickly!' Saying that that is it get out of here quickly is how Eleonora takes charge of the moment. Russian puts the key word right up front so her emotion lands on the first beat.
'No, I did not mean that for you.' Since he did not mean that for Ainura, Mikhail does not waste words on excuses.
'Yes, I am urgently selling a pony.' Here being urgently selling a pony sets up the next turn in their exchange.

'I sure am selling it, I am waiting for you.' Mikhail reminds Ainura that he sure am selling it he is waiting for Ainura before the moment passes. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Ainura, quickly clean everything up here.' With the shift and chaos in play, Eleonora keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'I came to work in Moscow.' Explaining that she came to work in Moscow lays the cards on the table for Eleonora.

'And now I am cleaning up after a horse.' Noting that she is cleaning up after a horse keeps Ainura's side of the story simple and clear. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Just as Eleonora finishes dealing with the pony disaster, she walks into the dining room and meets her supposed nephew Denis. See you next time!
